The Prophet recited Abraham's and Jesus's words about their people, raised his hands weeping for his Ummah, and Allah sent Gabriel to say He would please him regarding it.
A servant is nearest his Lord in prostration, so supplicate there; bowing and prostrating, the Prophet glorified Allah, asked forgiveness and sought refuge in His pleasure from His anger.
After bowing in prayer the Prophet asked Allah to rescue helpless Muslims, send famine on Mudar and curse other tribes, stopping once they were rescued or a verse came.
For a month in the dawn prayer, after bowing, the Prophet cursed Ri'l, Dhakwan, Lihyan and Usayya, who killed the seventy reciters at Bi'r Ma'una, and then abandoned it.
The Prophet recited Qunut in the dawn and evening prayers, and in prayer cursed Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and Usayya, saying Allah pardoned Ghifar and protected Aslam.
Every night there is an hour in which any Muslim who asks Allah for good in this world and the next is given it.
Rising to pray at night the Prophet praised Allah as Light and Lord of the heavens and earth and asked guidance and forgiveness, with set words for bowing and prostrating.
On Friday there is a short time when Allah grants any good a Muslim asks in prayer, placed by one report between the Imam sitting down and the prayer's end.
Over the dead, the Prophet asked Allah to forgive him, cleanse him of faults, admit him to the Garden and shield him from the torment of the grave and Fire.
Setting out, the Prophet said Takbir thrice and asked Allah for piety, ease and protection; returning from battle, Hajj or Umrah he said Takbir on high ground, praising his Lord.
The Prophet asked Allah, Revealer of the Book, to rout and shake the tribes, and at Uhud said if Allah willed, none would be left on earth to worship Him.
One should supplicate with resolve and conviction, never saying 'forgive me if You wish', for no one can compel Allah and nothing is too great for Him to grant.
A sick man had asked to be punished in this world instead of the Hereafter; the Prophet told him to ask for good in both and protection from the Fire.
The supplication the Prophet made most often asked Allah for good in this world and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire, and Anas included it in all his supplications.
The Prophet taught a desert Arab words of praise, and taught him and new Muslims to ask Allah for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, protection and provision.
The Prophet taught Abu Bakr a supplication for his prayer, confessing great wrong to himself and asking Allah, the Forgiving and Compassionate, for pardon and mercy.
Going to bed, one should lie on the right side entrusting oneself to Allah, to die on the fitra if death comes; other bedtime words praise Allah and seek protection.
The Prophet asked forgiveness, the setting right of his religion, world and Hereafter, guidance, chastity and a purified soul, said evening and morning supplications, and taught Ali to seek guidance.
Hearing a cock, ask Allah's favour, for it sees angels, and a donkey, seek refuge from Satan; in distress the Prophet affirmed Allah's oneness, Lord of the Throne.
A Muslim's supplication for his brother in his absence is answered, and the commissioned angel says Amen, may it be for you too.
A supplication is answered as long as one does not ask for sin or cutting kinship and does not grow impatient, saying he prayed unanswered and giving up supplication.
